analyte-resolved-fate:
Knowing where each named contaminant ends up, not just that the total is smaller.

Analyte-resolved contaminant fate means that for each named contaminant, the mass in each output stream is reported so that the mass leaving the process can be compared with the mass entering it. A total contaminant number cannot do this job, and a single favourable removal figure for one analyte does not transfer to another.
cellulose-acetate:
The plastic filter material most cigarette filters are made from.

Cellulose acetate is the thermoplastic material in the filter of a finished cigarette. Recovering it intact is the goal of the solvent-based routes; the washing and incorporation routes keep it physically intact but chemically unchanged. Its properties after any recycling route are not established for the material collected from cigarette filters, because no located source characterises the recovered polymer on a comparable basis.
dry-mass-basis:
A way of counting mass that does not change with how wet the material is.

A dry-mass basis states the mass of material excluding water, so that a wet lot and a dried lot of the same material can be compared. Without it, two reported splits can describe the same material, and a balance cannot be checked. Several published figures for this material do not state whether they were measured wet or dry.
four-field-sink:
The four things that must be located before a recovered material can be called a product.

The four fields are a dry-mass balance on a common dry-feed basis, analyte-resolved contaminant fate across the streams, a named final treatment route with a jurisdiction-specific acceptance basis, and a use-specific product gate that is independent of whether the mass balance closes. A method family that cannot locate all four is a hypothesis with a measurement plan attached, not a finished route.
heavy-metals:
Cadmium, lead, arsenic and mercury, treated as a stop condition rather than a parameter.

Heavy metals are treated throughout this layer as a stop condition rather than as a value to be averaged or traded off. A stream whose heavy-metal content has not been characterised cannot be routed to a product or to unclassified waste, and a favourable result on another criterion does not offset that.
microplastics:
Small plastic fragments produced when filters are handled or degraded.

The cellulose acetate filter is itself a source of microplastic fragments, and size reduction steps turn butts into a particle stream. Washing does not remove that potential, and partial biological degradation does not eliminate it. The magnitude is not measured in any located source.
nicotine:
The main soluble residue carried by the tobacco and the filter.

Nicotine is the best-studied contaminant of cigarette butts because it is soluble in water and is the residue most consistently described as being partly leached by washing. No located source reports nicotine removal efficiency for any recycling route on a stated mass basis, so the fraction removed remains unknown rather than small.
pah:
Combustion-derived compounds that many routes redistribute rather than remove.

Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons are the combustion residue most often described as being only partly transferred to the wash liquor. Because several routes simply encapsulate the butt material rather than treating it, the question for them is not removal but whether the compound can later escape the product.
tar:
The sticky combustion residue that binds other residues to the butt.

Tar and associated combustion residues are the fraction that makes washing difficult: they are only partly soluble in water and partly soluble in organic solvents, so no simple sequence of washes removes them completely. No located source quantifies what remains after any route.
tsna:
Carcinogenic compounds formed during tobacco combustion.

Tobacco-specific nitrosamines, of which NNN and NNK are the ones most often named, are part of the combustion residue carried by butts. They are named here because any credible measurement of contaminant fate has to include them; no located source reports their partitioning across any recycling route.
